goal: Build the SimplyCubed Code foundation: a gate-first, fake-engine-testable Go core so the full issue-to-PR loop runs with zero LLM spend, plus the written spec. Engine-dependent design (role prompts, budget/stall thresholds, Action packaging) is documented, not coded, because the blocked S3 Azure replay is what validates those assumptions.
invariants: claude-proposes-actions-dispose: the loop only ever opens a pull request; it never merges and holds no deploy credential.
gate-first: no milestone is done until `make check` is green, and it must be green at every commit, not only at the tip.
gate-required: a target repo with no `gate:` configured is refused; an ungated loop is not built.

no-secrets-in-repo: no session-private material (production-repo gaps, host credentials, Azure resource or deployment names, keys) enters this public repository. State the conclusion, never the private fact.
engine-independence: the loop, gate, config, state machine, and domain types compile and test without any real model call, behind a Runner interface with a deterministic fake.

milestones.title: Repo foundation, gate, and CI
doneWhen: .github/workflows/check.yml runs the gate (not a required check yet)

milestones.title: Domain types, Runner interface, fake engine
doneWhen: hermetic tests pass with no network

milestones.title: Gate runner, config, label state machine
doneWhen: internal/gate runs a repo gate command and captures exit code, output tail, and a normalized signature
internal/config loads .github/simplycubed.yml and refuses a config with no gate
internal/state models the sc: label lifecycle with mutual exclusion

milestones.title: Loop engine and the honesty test
doneWhen: internal/loop runs goal -> act -> grade -> repeat with a two-consecutive-red stop
the loop opens a pull request only on success (via a forge interface, faked in tests)
honesty test: a fake engine that never fixes the gate ends in Blocked and opens NO pull request

milestones.title: Engine-dependent design as ADRs (docs, not code)
doneWhen: ADRs for role prompt architecture, verdict schema rationale, budget and stall thresholds, GitHub Action packaging, and onboarding templates
each ADR marks itself as pending validation by the S3 Azure replay spike

blocked.reason: Needs the Azure OpenAI resource name, the gpt-5.4 and gpt-5.4-mini deployment names, and AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY provided by the user. Not to be worked around by reading any on-disk credential.

The high-signal spike: revert known-good commits in a real private target repo on branches and see whether a codex-on-Azure loop reproduces green-gate PRs. Blocked by S1. This is what M5's coded form waits on.

notes: First action of any continued pass: check whether the Azure key file exists (existence only, never read it). If it appeared, pivot to S1 then S2 before any further scaffolding.
